Here's what you need to know:<br/><br/>## Installation<br/><br/>Install nuqs with your package manager:[1]<br/>```<br/>npm install nuqs<br/>```<br/><br/>## Next.js Support<br/><br/>nuqs@^2 supports Next.js version `next@>=14.2.0` and works with both the app and pages routers.[1][3] For older Next.js versions, use nuqs@^1.<br/><br/>## Setup<br/><br/>### App Router<br/>Wrap your root layout with `NuqsAdapter`:[5]<br/>```tsx<br/>import \{ NuqsAdapter \} from 'nuqs/adapters/next/app'<br/><br/>export default function RootLayout(\{ children \}) \{<br/>  return (<br/>    <html><br/>      <body><br/>        <NuqsAdapter>\{children\}</NuqsAdapter><br/>      </body><br/>    </html><br/>  )<br/>\}<br/>```<br/><br/>### Pages Router<br/>Wrap your app in `_app.tsx`:[5]<br/>```tsx<br/>import \{ NuqsAdapter \} from 'nuqs/adapters/next/pages'<br/><br/>export default function MyApp(\{ Component, pageProps \}) \{<br/>  return (<br/>    <NuqsAdapter><br/>      <Component \{...pageProps\} /><br/>    </NuqsAdapter><br/>  )<br/>\}<br/>```<br/><br/>## Basic Usage<br/><br/>Replace `React.useState` with `useQueryState` to sync state with the URL:[4]<br/>```tsx<br/>import \{ useQueryState \} from 'nuqs'<br/><br/>export function Demo() \{<br/>  const [name, setName] = useQueryState('name')<br/>  return <input value=\{name \|\| ''\} onChange=\{e => setName(e.target.value)\} /><br/>\}<br/>```<br/><br/>You can provide default values and use parsers for type safety (like `parseAsInteger` for numbers).[4] |

  "markdown": "# useSearchParams\n\n@doc-version: 16.1.6\n@last-updated: 2026-02-16\n\n&#96;useSearchParams&#96; is a Client Component hook that lets you read the current URL's query string.\n\n&#96;useSearchParams&#96; returns a read-only version of the [&#96;URLSearchParams&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams) interface.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\n'use client'\n\nimport { useSearchParams } from 'next/navigation'\n\nexport default function SearchBar() {\n  const searchParams = useSearchParams()\n\n  const search = searchParams.get('search')\n\n  // URL -&gt; &#96;/dashboard?search=my-project&#96;\n  // &#96;search&#96; -&gt; 'my-project'\n  return &lt;&gt;Search: {search}&lt;/&gt;\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx\n'use client'\n\nimport { useSearchParams } from 'next/navigation'\n\nexport default function SearchBar() {\n  const searchParams = useSearchParams()\n\n  const search = searchParams.get('search')\n\n  // URL -&gt; &#96;/dashboard?search=my-project&#96;\n  // &#96;search&#96; -&gt; 'my-project'\n  return &lt;&gt;Search: {search}&lt;/&gt;\n}\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Parameters\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\nconst searchParams = useSearchParams()\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;useSearchParams&#96; does not take any parameters.\n\n## Returns\n\n&#96;useSearchParams&#96; returns a read-only version of the [&#96;URLSearchParams&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams) interface, which includes utility methods for reading the URL's query string:\n\n- [&#96;URLSearchParams.get()&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams/get): Returns the first value associated with the search parameter. For example:\n\n| URL | &#96;searchParams.has(\"a\")&#96; |\n| --- | --- |\n| &#96;/dashboard?a=1&#96; | &#96;true&#96; |\n| &#96;/dashboard?b=3&#96; | &#96;false&#96; |\n\n- Learn more about other read-only methods of [&#96;URLSearchParams&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams), including the [&#96;getAll()&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams/getAll), [&#96;keys()&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams/keys), [&#96;values()&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams/values), [&#96;entries()&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams/entries), [&#96;forEach()&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams/forEach), and [&#96;toString()&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams/toString).\n\n&gt; - If an application includes the &#96;/pages&#96; directory, &#96;useSearchParams&#96; will return &#96;ReadonlyURLSearchParams | null&#96;. from a Client Component must be wrapped in a &#96;Suspense&#96; boundary, otherwise the build fails with the [Missing Suspense boundary with useSearchParams](https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/missing-suspense-with-csr-bailout) error.\n&gt; - In development, routes are rendered on-demand, so &#96;useSearchParams&#96; doesn't suspend and things may appear to work without &#96;Suspense&#96;.\n&gt; \n&gt; Good to know:\n\n### Dynamic Rendering\n\nIf a route is [dynamically rendered](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/caching#dynamic-rendering), &#96;useSearchParams&#96; [How do you get search params from Page route (not API route) in Next.js v13.4+?](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/77748366/how-do-you-get-search-params-from-page-route-not-api-route-in-next-js-v13-4)<br/><br/># useSearchParams in Next.js<br/><br/>`useSearchParams` is a Client Component hook that lets you read the current URL's query string.[1][2] It returns a read-only version of the [`URLSearchParams`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/URLSearchParams) interface.<br/><br/>## Basic Usage<br/><br/>Import from `'next/navigation'` and use it in a Client Component:[2]<br/><br/>```tsx<br/>'use client'<br/><br/>import \{ useSearchParams \} from 'next/navigation'<br/><br/>export default function SearchBar() \{<br/>  const searchParams = useSearchParams()<br/>  const search = searchParams.get('search')<br/>  <br/>  // URL -> `/dashboard?search=my-project`<br/>  // `search` -> 'my-project'<br/>  return <>Search: \{search\}</><br/>\}<br/>```<br/><br/>## Key Methods<br/><br/>The hook provides read-only utility methods:[1][2]<br/><br/>- `get(param)` - Returns the first value of a search parameter<br/>- `has(param)` - Returns a boolean indicating if the parameter exists<br/>- `getAll()`, `keys()`, `values()`, `entries()`, `forEach()`, `toString()` - Additional URLSearchParams methods<br/><br/>## Important Considerations<br/><br/>- `useSearchParams` is **Client Component only** and not supported in Server Components to prevent stale values during partial rendering[2]<br/>- During static rendering, it returns `null` during pre-rendering and updates after hydration[1]<br/>- For Server Components, use the `searchParams` prop instead[2]<br/>- In App Router, if you need an object format, you can use `Object.fromEntries(searchParams)`[5]<br/><br/>## Benefits of URL Search Params<br/><br/>Using URL search params for search/filtering enables better analytics tracking, server-side rendering compatibility, and shareable/bookmarkable URLs.[3] |

**No.** The Next.js docs do not mention nuqs.

Findings:

1. **Search on nextjs.org** – A `site:nextjs.org nuqs` search returns no results.
2. **Search params docs** – The [useSearchParams](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) page only documents built-in APIs:
   - `useSearchParams` from `next/navigation`
   - The `searchParams` prop on Pages
   - Updating params via `useRouter` + `usePathname` or `Link` with a manual `createQueryString` helper

There is no reference to nuqs or any other third-party library for search params. The docs stick to the built-in primitives.

Setup for nuqs in Next.js 16 (App Router):

## 1. Install nuqs

```bash
pnpm add nuqs
```

`nuqs@^2` supports Next.js `>=14.2.0`, so it works with Next.js 16.

## 2. Add the adapter in the root layout

Wrap `children` with `NuqsAdapter` in `app/layout.tsx`:

```tsx
import { NuqsAdapter } from 'nuqs/adapters/next/app'

export default function RootLayout({
  children,
}: Readonly<{
  children: React.ReactNode;
}>) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body className={`${geistSans.variable} ${geistMono.variable} antialiased`}>
        <NuqsAdapter>
          <Toaster richColors position="bottom-right" />
          {children}
        </NuqsAdapter>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

Use the App Router adapter: `nuqs/adapters/next/app`.

## 3. Use in components

```tsx
'use client'

import { useQueryState } from 'nuqs'

export function SearchBar() {
  const [search, setSearch] = useQueryState('search')
  return (
    <input
      value={search ?? ''}
      onChange={(e) => setSearch(e.target.value)}
    />
  )
}
```

For multiple params with parsers:

```tsx
'use client'

import { useQueryStates, parseAsString, parseAsInteger } from 'nuqs'

export function FilteredGrid() {
  const [state, setState] = useQueryStates({
    section: parseAsString.withDefault('projects'),
    page: parseAsInteger.withDefault(1),
  })
  // ...
}
```

---

**Notes**

- Use `nuqs/adapters/next/app` for App Router.
- Use `nuqs/adapters/next/pages` for Pages Router.
- Use `nuqs/adapters/next` if you use both routers (slightly larger bundle).

Docs: [nuqs.dev/docs](https://nuqs.dev/docs) | [Adapters](https://nuqs.dev/docs/adapters) | [Basic usage](https://nuqs.dev/docs/basic-usage)
